messages.subject: Scantwo with few markers
parts:
Hi,

I am using the function scantwo with "mr" method with a subset of markers that are those for which scanone detected QTLs; 

I don't understand why in scantwo output there is some positions that are not in my initial set of marker and sometimes very far. With mr method should it not only test the markers provided and not try to find position along the genetic map ?

Also, the scanone output seems to provide only one interaction by pair of chromosome (c1:c1,c1:2, etc.). Can we retrieve all interactions ? 


Thanks, Emilien.

Could you give further details with exact code and results? It’s not clear what the problem is.
> Also, the scanone output seems to provide only one interaction by pair of chromosome (c1:c1,c1:2, etc.). Can we retrieve all interactions ?

The output of scantwo includes the detailed results, though not in a form that’s simple to work with. The summary function gives the single biggest result on each chromosome pair.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Scantwo with few markers
parts:
The output of scantwo is a list; the "lod" component is a matrix with the LOD score for the full model in the lower triangle and the LOD score for the additive model in the upper triangle. Get the interaction LOD score by subtraction. Here's an example:

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper)
out <- scantwo(hyper, method="hk", verbose=FALSE)

lod.int <- out$lod - t(out$lod)
lod.int[upper.tri(lod.int)] <- t(lod.int)[upper.tri(lod.int)]

lod.int[1:5,1:5]

karl
